Stoneware Pour-Over Coffee Set

A slow morning in one set: a ceramic dripper, a 600 ml carafe and two cups, thrown and glazed by hand in our small studio. Brews two cups in about four minutes.

What's in the box

  • Pour-over dripper (fits #2 paper filters)
  • 600 ml carafe with a no-drip spout
  • Two 240 ml cups

How do you brew with a pour-over?

Rinse the filter with hot water, add 22 grams of medium-fine coffee, pour 50 grams of water to bloom for thirty seconds, then pour slowly in circles until you reach 350 grams. The whole brew takes three to four minutes. Grind finer if it runs fast and coarser if it runs slow. Each piece is made from a dense stoneware clay that holds heat well, so your coffee stays warm while it drips. The glaze is food safe and lead free. Because every set is made by hand, the color varies a little from batch to batch, which is part of the charm.

Care

Dishwasher and microwave safe. Avoid sudden temperature changes, such as pouring boiling water into a cold cup straight from the fridge. Hand washing keeps the glaze glossy for longer.

Shipping and returns

Orders ship within two business days from our studio. Every set is packed in recycled paper and double boxed. If anything arrives damaged, send us a photo within 14 days and we will replace it. Unused sets can be returned within 30 days for a full refund. We ship to the United States and Canada, and shipping is calculated at checkout based on your address.

Why stoneware?

Stoneware is fired at a high temperature, which makes it dense, chip resistant and a good insulator. Compared with glass or plastic drippers it keeps the brewing temperature steady, which helps extraction. It is also heavier, so the dripper sits firmly on the carafe or on a mug while you pour. Our clay comes from a regional supplier and our glazes are mixed in the studio. We test every batch for leaching before it goes on sale. If you are new to pour-over coffee, this set is a simple, durable place to start, and it looks good on the counter between brews. Pair it with a gooseneck kettle and a burr grinder for the most consistent cup.
